# app-reviews v1.2.0

Answer reviews from code on both stores, read an app's versions from App Store
Connect, and pass credentials straight from a secret manager. This is a
backward-compatible minor release: existing code keeps its 1.1.0 behavior.

## Highlights

- **Credentials in memory.** `AppStoreAuth(key_id, issuer_id,
  private_key=pem_text)` and `GooglePlayAuth(service_account_info=mapping)`
  work without a key file. Each auth takes exactly one of its two sources.
  Neither shows the key in `repr`, and a validation error keeps it out of the
  frames an error reporter captures.
- **Replies.** `AppStoreReplies(auth)` and `GooglePlayReplies(auth)` take the
  same `proxy=`, `retry=`, `http=`, and `rate_limiter=` as the other clients:
  - `reply(review_id, text)` creates or replaces the reply. Play also needs
    `package_name=`.
  - `get_reply(review_id)` returns a `ReviewReply` or `None`.
  - `delete_reply(review_id)` exists on the App Store only, because Play has no
    delete API.

  Each has an async twin. `ReviewReply.state` is `"pending"` while Apple holds
  the reply back (for up to 24 hours) and `"published"` once it is visible.
- **Writes are never retried.** A reply is public and can't be recalled, so a
  write is sent exactly once whatever `retry=` says. The errors tell you what
  happened:
  - `ReplyOutcomeUnknownError`: a timeout, a dropped connection, or a 5xx after
    sending. Check `get_reply()` before you try again.
  - `ReplyRejectedError(reason)`: the store refused the reply, and nothing was
    published. A Play reply over 350 characters fails with
    `reason="too_long"` before anything is sent.
  - `RateLimitError(retry_after)`: a 429, with the wait the store asked for.
  - `AuthError`: the key can't be used or doesn't have the permission.

  Reads follow the normal retry policy.
- **Official App Store versions.** `AppStoreVersions(auth).versions(app_id)`
  returns `list[AppStoreVersion]` from App Store Connect, with each version's
  "What's New" text per locale. The official API has no release date field, so
  none is invented:
  - `created_at` is when the version was created in App Store Connect.
  - `earliest_release_date` is only the floor of a scheduled release.
  - `state` is `appVersionState`, which is `"READY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION"` once the
    version is live.

  For the dates versions reached the store, `AppStoreSearch.version_history()`
  is still the source.

## Permissions

| Store | Needs |
|---|---|
| App Store | An App Store Connect API key with the **Customer Support** or **Admin** role to reply. Reading versions needs a key that can see the app. |
| Google Play | The service account invited in Play Console with **Reply to reviews** for the app. |

## Endpoints

- App Store Connect:
  - [`POST /v1/customerReviewResponses`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/post-v1-customerreviewresponses)
  - [`GET /v1/customerReviews/{id}/response`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/get-v1-customerreviews-_id_-response)
  - [`DELETE /v1/customerReviewResponses/{id}`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/delete-v1-customerreviewresponses-_id_)
  - [`GET /v1/apps/{id}/appStoreVersions`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/get-v1-apps-_id_-appstoreversions)
- Google Play Developer API:
  - [`reviews.reply`](https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/reviews/reply)
  - [`reviews.get`](https://developers.google.com/android-publisher/api-ref/rest/v3/reviews/get)

## Migration

You don't need to change any code. To reply safely:

```python
from app_reviews import AppStoreReplies, ReplyOutcomeUnknownError

with AppStoreReplies(auth) as replies:
    if replies.get_reply(review_id) is None:
        try:
            replies.reply(review_id, "Thanks, this is fixed in 4.2.")
        except ReplyOutcomeUnknownError:
            pass  # check get_reply() later; do not blindly resend
```

`GoogleAuth` now takes a `GooglePlayAuth`, and the bare path it took before still
works.

## Compatibility

- Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14
- Runtime dependencies: `httpx>=0.28,<2` and `cryptography>=49`
- Typed package marker included

See the [changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md) and the
[Python API guide](../../docs/guide/python-api.md#replies).
